title: LC-MT370-ScopedOccupancyClaimsLeasesAndScheduling
clause: Coordinate project-qualified occupancy, claims, leases and scheduling across parallel Handshake agents and execution contexts.

scope.summary: GOAL: Integrate Locus with WP-1 multi-model orchestration so claims, occupancy and leases are canonical project-qualified SurrealDB records. A claim binds a Principal/model/session and execution context to one project/WP/MT target without making the workspace or session authoritative. Scheduling uses canonical readiness from MT-368/369, respects cross-project dependencies and project capacity policy, and remains safe under parallel models. Lease acquire/renew/release/expire/steal operations are transactional, fenced and EventLedger-correlated through MT-367.
acceptance_criteria: Claims and leases use project-qualified targets and bind owner Principal, model/session identity, execution context, epoch/fence, expiry and canonical revision.
Concurrent acquisition allows one valid owner per exclusive target; stale owners cannot renew, complete or release after a newer fence is issued.
Scheduling consumes canonical readiness and authorized dependency state, never GUI/taskboard projections or hidden remote details.
Session/workspace loss expires or recovers execution bindings without deleting project/WP/MT identity or terminal work receipts.
Cross-project parallel scheduling respects per-project policy and AccessSpace boundaries while remaining attributable, observable and recoverable.
proof_targets: Session crash, workspace loss and restart recovery tests
Argus multi-agent occupancy and conflict captures

enforcement_boundaries: Schedulers receive only authorized canonical readiness and occupancy.
Lease workers cannot widen project scope through a session or workspace binding.
same_project_private_resource_cases: A same-project agent outside a private AccessSpace cannot see, acquire or diagnose its protected work occupancy.
cross_account_negative_cases: Cross-account agents cannot claim, renew, release, schedule or infer another account's work.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Scheduler queues, occupancy UI and diagnostics retain the source claim/lease authorization scope.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Revocation or session/project context switch invalidates lease authority; stale fences cannot mutate the target.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Conflict messages do not reveal denied owner identity, model, session, lease timing, queue position or project label.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Record claim/lease/schedule transitions, fences, canonical target and anonymized conflict outcome.
Expose stale leases, renewal failures, occupancy conflicts, scheduler starvation and orphan execution bindings.
Record DEFERRED-with-reason if lease-stall and scheduler-starvation watchers are unavailable; never silently skip.

risk_if_missed: Parallel models can duplicate work, settle the wrong project's MT or retain authority after losing their lease.

risks: A stale owner completes after lease theft.
A session binding exposes another project.

research_provenance.source: Merged WP-1 MMO surfaces required by MT-361; MT-367/368/369 contracts; current MT executor/swarm/session models; established lease-fencing patterns and official SurrealDB transaction guidance.
research_provenance.selected_approach: Canonical scoped leases with fencing, project-qualified identity and readiness-driven scheduling.
